answer: Collateral-backed endorsement resists Sybil attacks: a new agent earns transaction weight only when established agents stake a deposit on its thread of past actions, and that deposit is slashed if the newcomer is later proven fake. A public beacon publishes periodic reputation checkpoints, and a summit of randomly selected auditors reviews disputed identities. Forging one fake is cheap, but buying endorsements for a thousand fakes means bribing or compromising many established agents and risking their deposits, so attack cost scales with the size of the swarm instead of staying near zero.
